idiom_name: plain object or class instance; === is reference identity
implementation_notes: JavaScript already implements the in-memory half of the pattern: === on objects is reference identity (two object literals with identical properties are not equal), and Object.is differs only for NaN and signed zero, so no equality machinery is needed as long as one object per entity is kept in memory. What remains is the identity field: carry a stable id (a UUID string or a branded id) on the object so an entity rebuilt from JSON, a database row or an API response can be recognised as the same thing, and keep state changes behind methods instead of replacing the object wholesale. When detached copies must compare equal, add an explicit equals/sameAs comparing ids, because the language does not let you redefine ===.
pitfalls: A JSON round-trip creates a new object, so === says false for the same customer; identity has to be re-established through the id and an explicit equals or a map keyed by id.
Object spread and Object.assign produce snapshots that look like entities but are detached; mutating either copy diverges silently and the last write wins.
== coerces types and Object.is differs on NaN and signed zeros; an ad-hoc equality built on either disagrees with identity semantics - compare ids with ===.
